protocol: National Trauma Triage Protocol (CDC Field Triage Guidelines)
purpose: A 4-step field decision scheme used by EMS to decide which injured patients need transport to a trauma center.
steps: Step 1 - Physiologic criteria: Measure vital signs and level of consciousness. Glasgow Coma Scale < 14, or systolic blood pressure < 90 mmHg, or respiratory rate < 10 or > 29 breaths/minute triggers transport to a trauma center.

Step 2 - Anatomic criteria: Assess anatomy of injury - penetrating injuries to head/neck/torso/proximal extremities, flail chest, crush/degloving/amputation injuries, pelvic fractures, paralysis, or two or more long-bone fractures trigger transport to a trauma center.
Step 3 - Mechanism of injury: Evaluate high-energy mechanisms - falls from height, high-risk auto crashes, pedestrian/bicycle struck, or motorcycle crash > 20 mph.

Step 4 - Special patient/system considerations: Consider age 55+, anticoagulant use, burns, end-stage renal disease, pregnancy > 20 weeks, or EMS provider judgment; when in doubt, transport to a trauma center.
